correctness.rationale: Exact q-ary interval probabilities give the arclength expression and positive deficit; the unique interior Chernoff tilt (strict convexity and relative-entropy derivative signs) centers finite supported increments with positive variance. Change of measure gives exact identities for deficit and per-refinement gain. Strict Jensen concavity yields positive gain. Standard lattice/nonlattice local limit theorems for exponentially decaying test functions yield the two sharp asymptotics. The beta integral is evaluated by independent substitutions and numerically cross-checked. The lattice correction is a positive absolutely convergent h-periodic sum. Finite checks were run from the embedded CHECK.py, independently comparing enumeration and multinomial grouping; they do not prove the infinite result. Assumptions, boundaries, and dependencies are explicit.

value.rationale: Pfeffer--Smith--Severa (2023, Section 5.1) explicitly asks to quantify additional arclength in each iteration. Resolving its sharp asymptotic gain for all fixed strictly positive nonuniform q-sided dice, identifying Chernoff information as the exponent, computing the beta prefactor, and treating the necessary arithmetic phase dependence are natural and nontrivial mathematical advances rather than isolated numeric samples. The resulting theorem is a usable exact leading law for the nested singular-CDF approximation process.
